notes.content: fill_helpers.rs: f2_fill (F2 smart F — from one boundary edge, follow the two neighbouring boundary edges to their far verts; quad (c,a,b,d) or triangle (a,b,c) if they coincide); auto_mirror (bisect by a WorkPlane keeping the -normal half, mirror it back with reversed winding, weld along the cut); bsurfaces (resample each stroke to  points, bridge consecutive strokes into a quad grid). 5 tests, clippy-clean.

description: Optional reuse path: wire outram-foam-basic-lib's LduMatrix + FvMatrix::solve_cg / solve_gamg (iterative sparse, FV face-addressing) as an ALTERNATIVE backend for outram-blender's large one-off sparse solves. Primary LA is faer (added 2026-07-17: dense + sparse Cholesky, better for interactive same-matrix/many-RHS mesh editing). The foam bridge is for code reuse within OUTRAM PARK on large iterative solves; note the impedance mismatch (foam ldu = cell-FACE addressing vs a vertex-vertex mesh Laplacian graph) and that foam has no sparse DIRECT factorization. Depends on the sparse-solve consumers existing first (op-hzs.1/.2 Laplacian/subdivision, plus future ARAP/parameterization).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: UNBLOCKED 2026-07-23: op-hzs.15 Laplacian smoothing is now a real sparse-solve consumer. Kept open as optional/low-value: the smoothing solve is symmetric, same-matrix, multi-RHS -> faer sparse Cholesky (direct) is the right fit and is implemented. foam LduMatrix is face-addressed, iterative-only (no direct factorization) -> impedance mismatch, strictly inferior here. Revisit only if internal solver code-reuse is specifically wanted.

title: outram-blender: optional bridge to outram-foam-basic-lib sparse solvers (CG/GAMG)

description:
Recorded 2026-08-11 so it is not lost. NOT diagnosed — I could not name the failing test, and I am not guessing at a cause.

WHAT HAPPENED: `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release` exited non-zero with

    error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p outram-mc-libs --lib`

That run was executing CONCURRENTLY with `cargo test -p njoy-outram-park-fork --lib --tests --release` in a separate process, both started at the same moment on the same machine.

WHY THE NAME IS MISSING: the invocation was piped through `grep -E '^(test result:|failures:|error|...)'`, which filtered out the per-test FAILED line before it was written to the log. My mistake in the harness, not the test's.

DID NOT REPRODUCE. Three subsequent runs with nothing else building:
- `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --release` -> 212 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (twice)
- `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release` -> 212 + 5 + 30 + 7 = 254 passed, 0 failed

PLAUSIBLE BUT UNPROVEN: the lib target holds the GPU tests (`gpu::surface_distance`, `gpu::xs_interp`, `gpu::batched_flight`, `gpu::union_grid`), and this host has a single NVIDIA RTX 3050. A second heavy build competing for CPU and memory, or two processes contending for the one GPU device, is the obvious suspect. But njoy's suite has no GPU tests, so a pure GPU-contention story is not clean, and a plain build-lock/CPU-starvation timeout is equally consistent with the evidence. Do not write either into a doc as the cause.

NEXT STEP IF IT RECURS: re-run WITHOUT a grep filter, capture the full log, and get the failing test name. Then decide whether the GPU tests need serialising (a test-level mutex or a `--test-threads` carve-out for the gpu module only — NOT for the whole suite, per the workspace rule against serialising slow suites).
title: outram-mc: one unreproduced test failure under concurrent cargo test load
